rows.note: Use 比賽 as the all-purpose noun for a competitive sporting event.

example.english: The football match is being held in Mong Kok tomorrow.
example.traditional: 聽日場足球比賽喺旺角舉行。
example.jyutping: teng1 jat6 coeng4 zuk1 kau4 bei2 coi3 hai2 wong6 gok3 geoi2 hang4

rows.note: Use 火柴 specifically for the small stick used to make a flame.

example.english: This match is damp and won't light.
example.jyutping: ni1 zi1 fo2 caai4 sap1 zo2 dim2 m4 zoek6

rows.note: Use 夾 as the all-purpose everyday choice when people, ideas, or interests go well together.

example.english: I match really well with Ah Ming.
example.jyutping: ngo5 tung4 aa3 ming4 gei2 gaap3 gaa3

rows.note: Use 對得上 when facts, figures, names, or other details correspond or tally with each other.

example.english: The figures on the bill match the bank record.
example.traditional: 張單嘅數字同銀行紀錄對得上。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 daan1 ge3 sou3 zi6 tung4 ngan4 hong4 gei2 luk6 deoi3 dak1 soeng5

rows.note: Use 襯 when matching colours, clothes, or other visually coordinated items rather than pairing objects into sets.

example.english: This blue shirt and these white trousers match well.
example.traditional: 呢件藍色恤衫同條白褲好襯。
example.jyutping: ni1 gin6 laam4 sik1 seot1 saam1 tung4 tiu4 baak6 fu3 hou2 can3

rows.note: Use 配對 when putting two items together as a correct pair, such as socks or cards.

example.english: We need to match the socks into pairs first, so don't mix them up.
example.traditional: 我哋要先配對啲襪，唔好搞亂。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 sin1 pui3 deoi3 di1 mat6 m4 hou2 gaau2 lyun6

rows.note: Use 配對 for two things regarded as a suitable matching pair or combination.

example.english: These two socks are a perfect match.
example.jyutping: ni1 loeng5 zek3 mat6 ngaam1 ngaam1 hou2 pui3 deoi3
